title: SpiffeId::provenance matches any path segment ending in via, not the documented via/{source}
description:
persona-core/src/spiffe_id.rs:91-102. The doc says it returns `Some(source)` if the path ends with `via/{source}`. The implementation tests `prefix.ends_with("via")`, which is true for any segment with that suffix:

    SpiffeId::new(td, "user/alice/servia/bob").provenance()   // Some("bob"), documented as None
    SpiffeId::new(td, "user/trivia/x").provenance()            // Some("x"),   documented as None

The `|| prefix == "via"` arm on the same line is dead — `"via".ends_with("via")` is already true.

This matters because provenance is what tells a relying party which identity source produced a claim; the real producer format is `user/{sub}/via/{source}` (persona-attestors/src/oidc.rs:89) where the source segment is attacker-influenced (it derives from the OIDC `sub`), so a `sub` ending in `via` yields a path whose provenance parses to an attacker-chosen tail segment.

Correct predicate: `prefix == "via" || prefix.ends_with("/via")`. Filing under docs-as-contract since the doc comment states the intended behaviour precisely and the code does not deliver it; may overlap with a correctness-review finding.
